scope: Proposition 4.11 (Local evolution and vacuum initialization) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The reduced equation (4.2), (4.22), with retarded feedback (4.21), has smooth local evolution for smooth initial wave data small in E10. It continues on finite time intervals while E10 remains bounded, the parameters stay in their chosen small range, the normalized acceleration and implicit-coordinate inverses stay uniformly controlled, and the spacelike and strict outflow margins remain positive. Smooth higher orders propagate on bounded time intervals; these higher seminorms need only be finite. For smooth vacuum constraint data, the initial lapse and shift derivatives can be chosen so that Υ and its first normal derivative vanish initially. The resulting evolution is vacuum.
